Need to search first.I couldn't write these notes, because my research didn't work and I have no source material.

**What happened:**
- My first attempts to open pages directly (enduringword.com/bible-commentary/esther-8/, preceptaustin.org's Esther 8 page, and biblehub.com's commentary pages for Esther 8:11 and 8:17) were all blocked. The tool will only open a page after it has appeared in search results.
- I then ran a batch of searches, but my code crashed on the first one before it saved any results.
- After that, the tool said I had used up all my research calls for this turn. So I never read a single page.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and leave out what I couldn't find. Since I found nothing, writing notes from memory would break those rules, so I haven't.

**What I'll do in the next turn:** if you reply "continue," I'll search first and then open the pages the searches return:
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word on Esther 8; BibleHub and StudyLight for Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Matthew Henry; Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon and Desiring God, Ligonier and The Gospel Coalition, and the Lutheran sites (LCMS and 1517). The likely points of difference are:
   - v. 8: why the first decree couldn't be cancelled, and what that says about God's law and the gospel
   - v. 11: whether it was right to kill women and children
   - v. 17: whether "became Jews" means real conversion or just fear
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes on vv. 9, 11 and 17; Bible Odyssey on how historical Esther is and on Purim; New Advent and Catholic.com on the Greek additions (the Catholic Bible's Esther includes the text of the king's second decree after 8:12).
